# Inlexzo (JNJ): the muscle-invasive bla: # Those rows are untouched. This adds only the failed SunRISe-2 unit

column10: share of the pool already in the base
column11: NCT04658862 (SunRISe-2) randomised 518 patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer who refused or were unfit for cystectomy to TAR-200 plus cetrelimab or chemoradiotherapy (ClinicalTrials.gov, read from the book's trials table). The label is BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive disease with carcinoma in situ (Drugs@FDA, NDA 219683, as jnj_inlexzo.csv records it), so none of this population is in the base
column12: no pool is seeded, because the programme has failed

column11: stopped for futility: Johnson & Johnson discontinued SunRISe-2 in October 2024 after the independent data monitoring committee's pre-specified interim analysis found TAR-200 plus cetrelimab did not show superiority to chemoradiotherapy (OncLive, 'Phase 3 Study of TAR-200/Cetrelimab Is Discontinued in MIBC', 2024-10-08; CancerNetwork, 2024-10-09). The final analysis, presented in 2026, did not improve bladder-intact event-free survival against chemoradiotherapy (Urology Times, 2026-03-01; J&J Medical Connect, 'INLEXZO SunRISe-2 study')
